mappings.title: Identities and credentials are managed
mappings.text: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Managed identities are the prerequisite for attributable privilege allocation under 01.c.
mappings.technical_validation_method: UID/GID shadow access check: enumerate account-to-resource ownership; flag orphaned UIDs and unmanaged service identities owning files.
mappings.citation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 2024), PR.AA-01
mappings.embedding_text: Identities and credentials are managed (PR.AA-01). Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization. | HITRUST anchor: 01.c Privilege Management - The allocation and use of privileges to information systems and services is restricted and controlled. Privileges are allocated on a need-to-use basis and only after formal authorization, applying the principle of least privilege; privileged access is tracked to an identified role or individual.

mappings.title: Access permissions incorporate least privilege and separation of duties
mappings.text: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties.
mappings.mapping_rationale: PR.AA-05 is CSF 2.0's consolidated privilege-management subcategory - define, manage, enforce, review with least privilege - a one-to-one match for 01.c.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Active Directory/host UID/GID shadow access check: enumerate file and directory ownership, group membership breadth, and world-writable or otherwise overbroad permission bits against a least-privilege baseline; flag orphaned owners and privilege sprawl.
mappings.citation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 2024), PR.AA-05

hitrust_control.control_title: Data Protection and Privacy of Covered Information

mappings.title: Legal and regulatory requirements including privacy are managed
mappings.text: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed.
mappings.mapping_rationale: 06.d sits in HITRUST's Compliance category; GV.OC-03 is CSF 2.0's home for managing legal/privacy obligations over covered information.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Scan profile binds each detector to its legal source (HIPAA identifier classes, PAN rules); findings are reported per-obligation in the compliance report, evidencing managed requirements.
mappings.citation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 2024), GV.OC-03
mappings.embedding_text: Legal and regulatory requirements including privacy are managed (GV.OC-03). Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed. | HITRUST anchor: 06.d Data Protection and Privacy of Covered Information - Data protection and privacy are ensured as required in relevant legislation, regulations, and contractual clauses. An organizational data protection and privacy policy is implemented and covered information (e.g., PII/PHI, cardholder data) is identified, minimized, and protected wherever it is stored or processed.

hitrust_control.control_title: Data Protection and Privacy of Covered Information

mappings.title: Confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
mappings.text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Protection of covered information at rest is the technical half of 06.d; entropy/chi-square analysis empirically verifies at-rest confidentiality protection.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Multi-attribute cryptographic pipeline: regex detection of PII/PHI/PAN patterns in traversed files combined with Shannon-entropy and chi-square tests to distinguish encrypted from plaintext storage; flag covered information found unencrypted or outside sanctioned locations.
mappings.citation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 2024), PR.DS-01
mappings.embedding_text: Confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected (PR.DS-01). An organizational data protection and privacy policy is implemented and covered information (e.g., PII/PHI, cardholder data) is identified, minimized, and protected wherever it is stored or processed.

mappings.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
mappings.text: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded.
mappings.mapping_rationale: ID.RA-01 is the CSF 2.0 statement of 10.m's identification-and-recording lifecycle for technical vulnerabilities.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Regex audit of service configuration files (SSH/TLS/web server) for weak ciphers, legacy protocol versions, and insecure directives; extraction of software version strings from package manifests and binaries for comparison against known-vulnerable version ranges.
mappings.citation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 2024), ID.RA-01
mappings.embedding_text: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded (ID.RA-01). Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded. | HITRUST anchor: 10.m Control of Technical Vulnerabilities - Timely information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use is obtained, the organization's exposure to such vulnerabilities is evaluated, and appropriate measures are taken to address the associated risk.

mappings.title: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed through their life cycles
mappings.text: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Lifecycle management of data - including end-of-life handling, re-use, and disposal - is 09.q's handling-procedures scope expressed in CSF 2.0 asset-management terms.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Recursive file-system traverser and ZIP archive chunker locate covered information across storage paths, including temp, recycle, and archive locations; entropy analysis detects residual plaintext sensitive data on paths staged for re-use or disposal.
mappings.citation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 2024), ID.AM-08
mappings.embedding_text: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed through their life cycles (ID.AM-08). mappings.title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
mappings.text: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring.
mappings.mapping_rationale: PR.PS-04 is CSF 2.0's audit-logging subcategory: generation plus availability of log records - the direct counterpart of 09.aa.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Audit Ledger Synthesis: every scan produces a tamper-evident kintsugi_scan.json evidence ledger; the scanner additionally verifies presence, permissions (via UID/GID module), and non-zero recency of host audit/syslog artifacts and logging daemon configuration files.
mappings.citation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 2024), PR.PS-04
